title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DALE'S HOUSEGUEST
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Dale Pruitt, an air conditioner repairman in Prescott, Arizona, who loves his quiet house.
Then his dad Clint, a seventy-nine-year-old retired rodeo clown, showed up with two suitcases and a saddle.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THREE CHAIRS
segments.quote: I had three chairs in my house; one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society.
segments.author: Henry David Thoreau
lines: Dale's living room had one recliner, and now Dad was in it.
Then Dale spotted his old copy of Walden, by Henry David Thoreau:
I had three chairs in my house; one for solitude, two for friendship, three for society.
Well, Dale had one chair. That was the problem.
So he drove to a yard sale and came home with two more.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE KEYS
segments.quote: You may be deceived if you trust too much, but you will live in torment if you do not trust enough.
segments.author: Frank Crane
lines: Next, Dad wanted to drive Dale's pickup to the hardware store.
Dale held the keys like they were a live rattlesnake.
Then he remembered a line from Frank Crane, an old newspaper writer:
You may be deceived if you trust too much, but you will live in torment if you do not trust enough.
He handed them over. Dad drove twenty miles an hour and waved at every cow.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE CHICKEN COOP
segments.quote: If a thing is worth doing, it is worth doing badly.
segments.author: G. K. Chesterton
lines: Dad got bored. Let's build a chicken coop, he said.
Dale said, We don't know how.
Dad grinned and quoted the English writer G. K. Chesterton:
If a thing is worth doing, it is worth doing badly.
So they built it badly. The door is crooked, and the hens love it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: ONE MORE RIDE
segments.quote: No wise man ever wished to be younger.
segments.author: Jonathan Swift
lines: Then the county rodeo called. Their clown broke his arm. Could Clint fill in?
Dale said, Dad, you're seventy-nine.
Dad put on his red nose and quoted Jonathan Swift, the Irish writer:
No wise man ever wished to be younger.
So Dale painted the clown barrel, and Dad practiced falling down on the lawn.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE OLD HURT
segments.quote: Forgiveness is not an occasional act; it is a permanent attitude.
segments.author: Martin Luther King Jr.
lines: The night before the rodeo, Dad said quietly, I missed all your ball games, son.
Dale had carried that for thirty years.
Then he remembered Doctor Martin Luther King Junior:
Forgiveness is not an occasional act; it is a permanent attitude.
So Dale said, I know, Dad. And he forgave him again the next morning, and the next.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: STAYING PUT
segments.quote: There is nothing like staying at home for real comfort.
segments.author: Jane Austen
lines: At the rodeo, Dad tumbled into his barrel, and the whole crowd roared.
Driving home, Dad said, I'll find an apartment and get out of your hair.
Dale thought of Jane Austen, the English novelist:
There is nothing like staying at home for real comfort.
So Dale said, Dad, you are home. And the third chair is yours.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Make room. Trust. Do it badly. Don't wish to be younger. Forgive. Come home.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Make room. Trust. Do it badly. Don't wish to be younger. Forgive daily. Come home.
My own dad tried to teach me to ride a horse once. The horse taught me instead.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
